relevant_to: all flavors; effective value is min(back_log, net.core.somaxconn) on Linux. Cannot matter when clients use a fixed connection pool established before the measured window (no connects during the run).

signals.metric: nstat TcpExtListenOverflows and TcpExtListenDrops (/proc/net/netstat) deltas during the run
signals.condition: > 0 during the measured window
signals.why: SYNs/ACKs are dropped when the accept queue of the listen socket is full; clients retry after 1s+ SYN retransmit timeouts.

signals.metric: ss -ltn: Recv-Q vs Send-Q of the mysqld listen socket (current accept queue vs its limit)
signals.condition: Recv-Q reaches Send-Q during connect bursts
signals.why: Send-Q shows the effective backlog; a full queue means drops.

signals.condition: near-zero connects/s during the window
signals.why: without connection churn the accept queue is never used.

impact_bound: At most the time clients lose to SYN retransmits (>=1s per dropped connect) times dropped connects; zero with persistent connections. Typical: none for pooled benchmarks; high only for connect-per-request workloads with bursts.

experiment.change: raise back_log (and net.core.somaxconn to at least the same value), restart
experiment.predict: TcpExtListenOverflows/ListenDrops delta -> 0; connect latency p99 drops
experiment.confirm_or_refute: no drops after change confirms; if drops were already 0 the change cannot help
experiment.cost_or_risk: restart; slightly more kernel memory for queued connections

collected: no: add nstat TcpExtListenOverflows/TcpExtListenDrops deltas and ss -ltn listen-socket queue sampling
